title: Dramatic twist as vile hate video nurse is rushed to hospital - while Israeli influencer posts FULL unedited clip of antisemitic rant after detectives were kept waiting 48 hours
text:
By Ashley Nickel for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 23:52 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 00:03 GMT, February 14, 2025
One of the dishonored nurses who threatened to kill Israeli patients has been transferred to the hospital during the night with mental health problems.
The news of the hospitalization of the pediatric nurse Ahmad Rashad Nadir on Thursday night occurs when the influencer of Israeli social networks Max Veifer released its interview without editing with Nadir and the colleague Sarah Abu Lebdeh.
Veifer shared the images on Instagram shortly before the 10 am on Friday after detective applications in the last 48 hours to share the unprocessed video.
Veifer said that NSW’s police had not told him where to send the video, delaying his release.
The video shows the two West Sydney nurses at Bankstown Hospital who boast of killing Israeli patients, while they are inside the installation on Tuesday.
“It’s the country of Palestine, not your country, you’re a piece of shit,” said Abu Lebdeh.
“One day your time will come and you will die the most horrible death.”
Veifer questioned if the couple would treat an Israeli patient who seeks attention, but the woman cut it by saying: “I will not treat them, I will kill them … I don’t want God, I hope God.”
“You have no idea how many (Israelis) came to this hospital and sent them to Jahannam (hell),” said Nadir, while making a gesture that slides his throat.
Ahmad Rashad Nadir (in photo 0 was hospitalized two days after threatening to ‘kill’ Israeli patients
Nadir and Collega Sarah Abu Lebdeh (in the photo together) boasted to kill Israeli patients at West Sydney hospital at Bankstown hospital
Veifer shared the full video, saying: ‘The police are asking me for the unpaid version. I have nothing to hide.
“Here is and if they tell me where to send it, I will send them to them.”
The NSW police confirmed that the emergency services were called to Nadir Bankstown’s house shortly before 9 pm on Thursday night after reports of a ‘concern for well -being’.
He was taken to the hospital for additional evaluation.
Both Nadir and Abu Lebdeh were deregisting to practice anywhere in Australia by the Nursing and Partern Board of New South Wales on Thursday.
“As a result, the Australian Health Professional Regulation Agency has automatically updated its history in the Public Registry of Professionals,” said Federal Minister of Health, Mark Butler.
‘As a result, this means that the two nurses cannot practice nursing anywhere in Australia, in any context.
‘Australians have the right to feel safe wherever they go and nowhere should be safer than a hospital.
“His disgusting comments, and the hatred that supports them, takes place in our health system and there is no place in Australia.”
Abu Lebdeh and Nadir apologized for their comments after their hate speech went viral.
More to come.
